dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Listen, I'm not one to begrudge people a little secret here and there...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: But, this... is taking it a bit far, don't you think?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How do you like it here?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: It's wonderful. There's simply nothing I could complain about.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Well... Except for that fact that it borders on being too comfortable. The urge to lie down and abandon my responsibilities is hard to resist...

choices.text: Well, I want people to be able to relax here.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Hm, I can see that. But I'm afraid that's a foreign concept to me.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Whether it's Nod-Krai or my far-off homeland... Peace of mind doesn't exactly come with the territory.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Hehe, quite the open book, aren't you... I can tell what you're thinking: "What does she have to complain about? She just sends Jahoda to do her dirty work."

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Just messing with you. The most I got from that smile was that you're in a good mood. So what's the reason? Struck it big on a commission?

choices.text: No, Paimon promised to start handling breakfast from now on.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Haha, is that so? Well, then the little one needs to be trained well. I'm sure Aino could help, if she needs specialized, Paimon-sized cooking equipment.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: In any case, your travel companion finally agreed to start splitting the chores, huh? Aiming for a better work-life balance?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You should take a break every now and then too, Nefer.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: You're preaching to the choir. Too bad I've got everyone in Nod-Krai, including my boss, gunning for the exact opposite.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: That said... Save me a room here, just in case. Who knows, maybe I'll get a chance for a real break someday.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: And when that day comes... Ah, on second thought, better not say the last part out loud, or it won't come true.

choices.text: Actually, it's been pretty light on the commission-front lately...

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Nothing wrong with that. A good work-life balance makes you more productive in the long run.

choices.text: Slacking off is what this place is for.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Would you like to have a chat with me?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Of course. What do you want to talk about? The wanted criminals in Nod-Krai with the highest bounties? The secret lingo of the black market? Or maybe... Oh! Did you need to get your hands on some under-the-table armaments?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Um... how about something more normal? Like your daily life...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Huh... that's not a "normal" topic for me. Not a lot of people come to me for a casual chat, so... I'm not sure what to say.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Well, what do you and Jahoda usually talk about?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: The commissions she messes up, how to salvage the commissions she messes up... what sort of commissions she'll mess up in the future.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: And other things, of course, like... her paycheck, who needs to watch the storefront, who's going to feed Ashru...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Ah, but I'm tabling that last one for now. Jahoda's too generous with the food, and Ashru's been getting chubby.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: I'm thinking about ordering a cat-sized hamster wheel from Aino to help Ashru slim back down.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Friends? Hah, I've got plenty of those. Why, interested in meeting some of these "friends" of mine? I can introduce you to them sometime...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Real friends, I mean...

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: I am talking about real friends. These ladies and gentlemen are esteemed guests of the Curatorium. Our friendship has inspired many a generous financial donation on their part.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: It's a friendship that will remain unbreakable... Until they run out of Mora, at least.

choices.text: That just makes them your customers!

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: At the Curatorium, the line between "guests" and "friends" is a thin one indeed.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: After all, we deal in goods that cannot be seen or touched — there are no guarantees in a business like that.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Without a solid friendship and the level of trust that comes with it, how could I convince my guests to part with their precious Mora?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So how does one establish that sort of "friendship"?

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: How indeed. Hmm... I'll skip over the tricks of the trade. The most important thing is to find "common ground."

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Shared hobbies or habits. A common friend... or a common enemy. Similarities, you see, are the source from which friendship flows. And, with a few nudges in the right direction, it can be nurtured into a rushing river.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Of course, if you alone control the "source"... you alone control the entire river of friendship.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: And that means... whether the river remains clear or turns muddy, flows freely or dries up... is all in your hands.

choices.text: I don't want to control my friendships.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Yes, I can see that... I'm sure that's part of what people find so endearing about you.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Still, it's best to be careful. I've seen people bare their soul... only for it to be sold to the highest bidder.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: If you ever meet someone you can't read, feel free to ask me. I'll help you separate the loyal ones from the snakes waiting to strike while your back is turned.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: But don't worry. No matter how well-hidden they think they are, they'll never escape my gaze.

choices.text: I prefer friendships to happen naturally.
Do you have other friends in Nod-Krai?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is there anything you'd like to do?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Hm... This place is cut off from the outside world, right? Strangers can't just slip in and out?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yeah, I guess...?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Perfect. I'm going to borrow a room to write a few letters.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: It's not everyday I get to stay in a place that keeps its own secrets. I'd be a fool not to take advantage of it.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: You have no idea the lengths I go to keep my correspondences confidential. If there's so much as a fly nearby, I'll snatch it out of the air before I put pen back to paper.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: After all, my "friends" are watching my every move, fangs bared, just waiting for a chance to step on me to get to the top.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Of course, none have succeeded... Heh, much to their own chagrin. The fall from grace can leave more than just a bruised ego in its wake...

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: But, even at rock bottom, some refuse to quit the game... I suppose I admire them, in a way.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Not the sharpest tools in the shed, or the strongest — but they've got tenacity, I'll give them that. People like that don't often rise to the top, but they survive.... and that's something.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Well, I should get writing. Oh, and I might stop by this realm of yours from time to time going forward.

response.speaker: Nefer
response.text: Ah... But, commandeering a room like that was rather rude, wasn't it... If you'd like to collect rent, we can settle the bill every three months. How's that sound?

choices.text: I mean, feel free. But why...?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Good morning, Nefer.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Well, it certainly is for me, but you still seem half-asleep... How about a riddle to get the neurons firing?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Haha, just kidding. No one in their right mind would want to start off the day with mind games. Here, have some warm water, it'll perk you right up.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Good night, Nefer.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Oh, yes. Good night. I didn't realize it was so late already. Go get some sleep... I still have some matters to attend to.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: This house indeed resembles the style preferred in Nasha Town... It's missing a bit of that authentic flavor, though.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Where are the opportunists scheming in their rooms, the adventurers nursing dreams of greatness, the sacks of jingling, clinking Mora...?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: What I'm trying to say is — how am I supposed to put my talents to work?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: You've really gone out of your way to replicate my humble little shop.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: What's more... without Ashru to rearrange them, the books on these shelves are a lot neater than the ones back in Nasha Town.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: You're wondering why Jahoda doesn't tidy them up? Ah, well, Ashru's too fast for her — she can't straighten them up as quickly as he can knock them down.
